title: New Orleans feeling versus bands on the road
summary: Musicians on the road lacked the feeling of New Orleans players, who admired him.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: There wouldn't be a band from here that would be made up here. How did the music compare away from here, some of those bands with the fellows from around here? Did they have as much swing to it?

Some of those bands, they had nice bands out there. They were nice swinging bands. But I don't know, none of those bands out there would swing like they were doing, like the musicians from the deep south. They would play, they would do wonderful music, but they didn't have the feeling the musicians from New Orleans had. Or from Baton Rouge or from down here. They just didn't have the feeling. But they played, they were good musicians playing. But it looked like all of New Orleans musicians, the musicians close around New Orleans territory, had a better, greater feeling than a lot of guys you would meet on the road. They admire you. They'd say, man, you come from New Orleans? I said, yeah, I come from New Orleans. I like the way you play. I like your style. I like your feeling. But I run into a lot of good musicians out there. But all the musicians I've seen, I've played with out there, met out there. And it seems to me that none of them had the feeling a guy had from New Orleans. Like the guys just from this part of the country had more feelings towards music. Like the guy from here put his whole heart and soul in music.
